hero_subtitle: Explore how Rochdale Metropolitan Borough Council manages public money. Reform UK won 14 of 60 seats (23%) at the 7 May 2026 election — a significant breakthrough but not the largest party. Full transparency data coming soon.
publisher_bio: This website was created by Tom Pickup, Reform UK county councillor for Padiham and Burnley West and Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care at Lancashire County Council. He is also parish councillor for Clowbridge with Dunnockshaw. Tom builds transparency tools that make public spending data easier to check.

publisher_quote: It's your money. The more people understand where it goes, the better.

political_control.tenure_note: May 7 2026 result: Reform UK won 14 of 60 seats (23%) — significant breakthrough but not the largest party. 2nd party (Reform): Lab.

doge_context.political_control: Reform UK breakthrough — 14/60 seats (23%) at the 7 May 2026 election. Not largest party.

spend_triangulation.note: Transparency gross = £4.13B across every class in the published corpus. Procurement-paid (discretionary third-party payments) = £3.82B. Non-procurement rows: Care-Act redacted direct payments to individuals (£297.5M), statutory pass-throughs (£4.2M) — all excluded from third-party-supplier forensic analyses. Net revenue budget figures (where published) are smaller again because they net capital, grants received, and reserves movements — transparency totals include all of these.

procurement_paid.note: Discretionary third-party supplier payments — the real procurement footprint.

direct_payment_individual.note: Care Act 2014 + UK GDPR redactions — foster carers, SGO recipients, ASC service-user direct-payment holders. Lawfully unnamed.

statutory_pass_through.note: DSG to schools, BCF to NHS ICB, PFI unitary charges, DFG to districts, concessionary travel. Authority has no procurement discretion.
